why: An unbolded label with a language note, such as "Mr Chan Sun Wing (In Mandarin):", starts that member's turn; a bare "Mr Tan:" without the note stays inside the speech.
title: INDUSTRIAL UNREST
html:
Sitting Date:19-03-1962
Title:INDUSTRIAL UNREST


Column: 322

INDUSTRIAL UNREST


    Dr Lee Siew Choh (Rochore): Mr Speaker, Sir, I support the amendment.

    Mr Chan Sun Wing (Upper Serangoon) (In Mandarin): Mr Speaker, Sir, looking at the amendment put forward by the Government, I feel that it is rather ridiculous.

    They have been enchanted according to the Chinese.

    Mr Speaker: Order. Mr Serjeant-at-Arms, will you see that order is kept in the Gallery?

    Mr Chan Sun Wing (In Mandarin): I believe that if the Government accept my suggestion they will then calm down.

    Mr Speaker, Sir, now I am going back to the motion itself. A worker told me:

    Mr Tan: "We will not go back."

    Inche Rahamat(In Malay): This is related to my question.

    The Prime Minister (In Mandarin): I am an elected Prime Minister.
